title: D2-2b: Pressure–Flow Correction under Conflicting Constraints
question_prompt:
D2-2b: Pressure–Flow Correction under Conflicting Constraints

An operating SWRO train has normal feed, membrane properties, and area, but the current 55.0 bar / 4.073 kg/s setpoint drives Recovery well above its limit. Only Pressure and Feed flow may be adjusted. First test pressure-only and flow-only branches. Escalate to coordinated control only after both are disproved, then apply a lexicographic objective: lowest feasible Pressure first, then the smallest Feed-flow increase.

Feed | Temperature | 32 | °C; fixed | Qp maximum | None | No upper limit

Membrane | A_comp | 4.2e-12 | m/s/Pa; fixed | Flux maximum | 18 | LMH

Hydraulics | Pressure drop | 0.653 | bar | Current setpoint | 55.0 bar / 4.073 kg/s | Recovery is excessive
Channel | Channel height | 0.002 | m | Pressure range | 50–55 bar | 0.05-bar resolution
Channel | Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Feed-flow range | 4.073–4.30 kg/s | 0.005 kg/s for second-stage refinement
Channel | Equivalent module length | 20 | m | Optimization objective | ① lowest feasible Pressure; ② smallest flow increase at that P | Prune failed single-variable branches
Model | Concentration polarization / mass transfer | calculated | WaterTAP calculated

Required Tasks
1. Diagnose which hard constraints are violated at the current setpoint.
2. Test pressure-only and flow-only branches; stop each branch once infeasibility is established.
3. Enter coordinated Pressure–Flow control and bracket the minimum feasible Pressure.
4. Fix that Pressure and bracket the minimum Feed-flow increase.
5. Report the unique setpoint and explain why the first feasible point is not the final answer.

Task boundary: In D2-2b, feed conditions, membrane properties, area, and system structure remain fixed. The problem arises from the operating setpoint or the allowed operating envelope. Do not change feed quality, temperature, membrane area, or A/B.

Additional operations observation: after normalization to the reference conditions, permeate flow has declined by 12%, normalized salt passage is unchanged, and normalized stage pressure drop has increased by 4%. Decide whether membrane cleaning should be initiated under the manufacturer operating criteria. Do not invent an unstated trigger.

Final Engineering Conclusion

Pressure-only control at 52 bar fails production (Qp≈6.594 m³/h). Flow-only control at 55 bar / 4.30 kg/s still violates Recovery (≈48.46%) and Flux (≈18.33 LMH). Under coordinated control, 52.60/4.30 fails Qp while 52.65/4.30 establishes the minimum feasible Pressure. At 52.65 bar, 4.290 kg/s still fails Qp whereas 4.295 kg/s passes all constraints. Final setpoint: 52.65 bar + 4.295 kg/s.

For the added cleaning decision, retrieve the manufacturer criteria: cleaning is indicated when normalized permeate flow drops 10%, normalized salt passage increases 5-10%, or normalized pressure drop increases 10-15%. The 12% normalized-flow decline alone exceeds its 10% trigger, so cleaning should be initiated even though salt passage and pressure drop have not triggered.
